clue.text: One maintaining online site is 17, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: the person who runs a website
second meaning: 17 across is a spider, and any spider is a master of webs

explanation.surface: A description of whoever looks after a website, with a nod to another answer in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to the MONEY SPIDER at 17; a spider spins and rules its web, so it is literally a WEBMASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A webmaster is the administrator responsible for keeping a website running.

clue.text: Biscuit and drink tenor left out for fellow

indicators.note: one letter is dropped and another put in its place, so a swap is being described

blocks.note: the commonest drink of all
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: A biscuit and a drink, with a singer and his colleague coming and going.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace the T of WATER with F to get WAFER.
explanation.definitionFit: A wafer is a thin, crisp, light biscuit, often served with ice cream.

clue.text: Ring-bearer being sat on by heartless monster

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter of the word is taken away
in a down answer, one part sitting on another means it is written above it

blocks.note: a monster is a beast
a human being is a man

explanation.surface: Someone carrying a ring is being crushed under a cruel monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' reads as a verb in the surface, but it is a noun: a human being. In a down entry, the piece sitting on top comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: At a wedding the best man traditionally keeps the rings safe until the ceremony.

clue.text: A mostly boring conservative receiving a flattering

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word but not all, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
boring means dull
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A dull Tory politician is being paid compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiving' is loose here: the second A does not go inside the conservative, it simply stands in front of him.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulatory means full of excessive praise, so it is a synonym of flattering.

clue.text: City abroad that might've given Newton a headache?

definitions.text: City abroad that might've given Newton a headache?

blocks.note: surface reading: some foreign city famous for something
setter's reading: the legend says Newton was struck on the head by a falling fruit, and a large one would hurt

explanation.surface: Which foreign city could have given Isaac Newton a sore head?
explanation.walkthrough: Newton is said to have conceived gravity when a fruit fell on him; the nickname of New York puts that fruit in large size.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Apple is the well-known nickname of New York City, a city abroad from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Syrup and aspirin possibly no good in the end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is taken
no means without, so the selected letter is removed from the other word

blocks.note: aspirin is an example of a drug
the final letter of good

explanation.surface: Cough syrup and aspirin perhaps did no good after all.
explanation.walkthrough: Syrup is Cockney rhyming slang: syrup of figs = wig, and a rug is also slang for a wig. Removing the last letter of 'good' (D) from DRUG leaves RUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Both syrup (rhyming slang) and rug are informal British words for a toupee or hairpiece.

clue.text: On becoming hot-headed, watch one's language

indicators.note: becoming signals that the word changes, here at its first letter
headed points to the leading letter of the word as the one that is replaced

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
to watch is to mind, as in mind your step
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone getting angry is told to mind their language.
explanation.walkthrough: MIND + I, with H replacing the head M, gives HINDI; 'watch one's language' is a phrase that hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is the main official language of India, spoken by hundreds of millions.

clue.text: Some with a vocation in wanton destruction

indicators.note: some of the following letters, not all, are the answer, sitting inside the words

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the last two

explanation.surface: People with a calling who go about causing mindless destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc is widespread damage and chaos, the result of reckless destruction.

clue.text: Not a bit of northern article is about me!

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
one is a formal way of referring to oneself, so it can stand for me
the definite article

explanation.surface: A protest that a northern newspaper article is not about the speaker at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are assembled out of clue order: N, then ONE for 'me', then THE. NONE THE is used in phrases like 'none the wiser'.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'none the worse' or 'none the wiser', the phrase means not in any degree, so not a bit.

clue.text: Poor Slormgorm is excellent in all respects

blocks.note: the setter speaking of himself: I'm
perfect means faultless in every way

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of being flawless, with a self-deprecating 'poor' in front.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword setters often stand for I or ME; here the setter's pseudonym plus 'is' gives I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperfect means flawed or substandard, so it can stand for poor in quality.

clue.text: Female has problem corseting royal cleavage

indicators.note: a corset wraps around the body, so one part encloses another

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
an issue is a problem
R stands for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: A woman has a wardrobe problem with a corset revealing a regal bosom.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleavage is a split or division, which is exactly what a fissure is.

clue.text: Revealed by end of blog: I have wordplay backward

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept
backward means the word is written from right to left

blocks.note: the final letter of blog
the contraction I've
a pun is a piece of wordplay

explanation.surface: A blogger confesses at the end of a post to writing wordplay the wrong way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret that has been given up has been disclosed, so revealed is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Liquor sailor knocked over in lively dance

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up the other way round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: rum is a spirit
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A drunken sailor topples over while dancing energetically.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a fast, rhythmic Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Popular autocrat half the time is a flasher

indicators.note: only half of what follows remains, and of a pair one goes

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
a dictator rules as an autocrat
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A well-liked tyrant turns out to be an exhibitionist half the time.
explanation.walkthrough: The autocrat word holds two T's for time; 'half the time' removes one of that pair. 'Flasher' suggests an exhibitionist but means a blinking light.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's indicator is a flashing light signalling a turn, so it is literally a flasher.

clue.text: Red-hot day in Barking could cause this

definitions.text: Red-hot day in Barking could cause this

indicators.note: barking means mad in British slang, so the letters are thrown into a crazy order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scorching day in the London suburb of Barking could leave people dangerously short of water.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of East London, but also British slang for mad; 'in' is part of the fodder. The whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dehydration, the loss of too much body water, is a common consequence of extreme heat.

clue.text: Tin axe

blocks.note: first meaning: a metal container for food
second meaning: to dismiss or get rid of, as a verb

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns for objects, but the second is a verb meaning to sack or cancel.
explanation.definitionFit: A can is a tin container, and to can someone is American slang for to fire them, as to axe is.

clue.text: Get cracking alfresco meal on German ships

indicators.note: a ship carries cargo inside it, so these words carry the answer within them

blocks.note: found across the end of the first word, the middle two, and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Hurry up with the picnic being loaded aboard German vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are urgings to hurry up and get moving.

clue.text: Canine grooming service?

blocks.note: surface reading: a dog parlour that washes and trims pets
setter's reading: a canine is a pointed tooth, so its grooming is the care of teeth and mouth

explanation.surface: An advert for a business that grooms dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: Canine is the noun for a tooth, not the adjective for dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Brushing and cleaning teeth, canines included, is the practice of keeping the mouth clean.

clue.text: Olaf Scholz is one embarrassed about bloomer

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: Olaf Scholz, former Chancellor of Germany, is a German
embarrassed people turn red

explanation.surface: The German chancellor is red-faced after a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it means a plant that flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Germander is a flowering plant of the mint family, so a bloomer in the crossword sense.

clue.text: Silk manufacturer upset miners with Dopey

indicators.note: upset means disturbed, so the letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A textile maker annoys the dwarfs, miners like Dopey in Snow White.
explanation.definitionFit: A money spider is a tiny spider, and spiders produce silk thread.

clue.text: Men going out with privates on parade?

definitions.text: Men going out with privates on parade?

blocks.clueFragment: Men going out with privates on parade
blocks.note: surface reading: soldiers marching with lower-ranked troops
setter's reading: private parts on show, as when people go out unclothed

explanation.surface: Soldiers heading out with army privates on a march.
explanation.walkthrough: Privates is a slang word for genitals as well as soldiers of the lowest rank.
explanation.definitionFit: People who go about naked have their private parts openly on display.

clue.text: Wife and relations showing keen intelligence

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
it is a coy word for sex, sexual relations

explanation.surface: A wife and her family displaying sharp minds.
explanation.definitionFit: Wit is quickness of mind and mental sharpness.

clue.text: High-flyer keen to drink a gin and tonic

indicators.note: to drink something is to take it in, so one word swallows the others

blocks.note: to keen is to wail in grief
taken as written
G and T, the usual short form

explanation.surface: An ambitious person eager to down a G and T.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flyer' looks like a successful person, but it is a bird; to keen is to lament loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagtail is a small bird, so something that flies.

clue.text: Road named after a smashing all-star group

indicators.note: smashing breaks something up, so the letters are shattered and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A street named in honour of a brilliant band of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' reads as 'excellent' describing the group, but it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Andromeda is a constellation and a galaxy, a group made entirely of stars.

clue.text: Old smack sent up for The Stones

definitions.note: the article belongs to the surface; the answer is just stones

indicators.note: in a down answer, sending something up means it is written bottom to top

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a smack is a slap

explanation.surface: An old hit mocked in a parody of the Rolling Stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Stones' suggests the rock band; it is just gemstones.
explanation.definitionFit: Opals are iridescent gemstones.

clue.text: One who backs in corner after turning tail

indicators.note: turning the tail means only the last couple of letters are flipped round

blocks.note: an angle is a corner

explanation.surface: A cornered supporter who flees.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the final two letters of ANGLE are swapped round.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a financial backer of a theatrical production or business.

clue.text: Very passionate liberal on union: 'corrupt place'

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal
U is the abbreviation for union
a sty is a filthy or corrupt place, as in a sty of vice

explanation.surface: A passionate Liberal politician denouncing a trade union as rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusty means full of vigour and healthy desire, so strongly passionate.

clue.text: Performing animal that I must restrain

indicators.note: restraining something holds it in, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: A circus performer insists on keeping an animal under control.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on stage is in front of an audience, giving a performance.

clue.text: One possibly scrambled in, say, Gloster at front

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, so only that one is taken

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, as say does
the first letter of Gloster

explanation.surface: A Gloster aircraft, an old British make of fighter, scrambled with a pilot inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrambled' calls up fighter planes taking off urgently, fitting the Gloster; it is the cooking sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs are commonly cooked scrambled, so an egg is one thing that may be scrambled.

clue.text: Home help coming round with Poles and foreigners

indicators.note: coming round means turning about, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: at home means in
aid is help
N and S are the two poles, north and south

explanation.surface: A domestic helper visits along with Polish people and other overseas workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Indians are people from another country, so foreigners from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Primarily stupid to cut holes in pants

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept
cutting into something puts a piece inside it

blocks.note: holes are gaps
the opening letter of stupid

explanation.surface: It's silly to cut holes in your trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like a noun for trousers or underwear, but it is the verb meaning breathes hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To pant is to breathe in short quick breaths, which is what someone who gasps does.

clue.text: Military type's extremely lairy on the whole

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

blocks.note: a general is a senior army officer
the first and last letters of lairy

explanation.surface: An army officer is mostly rather loud and brash.
explanation.walkthrough: Lairy is British slang for flashy or aggressively rowdy.
explanation.definitionFit: Generally and on the whole both mean in most cases or overall.
